subject: Telemetry & logs: PII redaction options + evidence request
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@medicohealth.com>
Cc: Amir Qureshi <amir.qureshi@medicohealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-11T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Telemetry & logs: PII redaction options + evidence request

Hi Lina / Amir,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good discussion and appreciate the level of detail from your security and platform teams. I wanted to capture the post-call recap and clearly list the asks we discussed so you can share with Procurement/SecOps.

Recap (high level)
- Scope: MedicoHealth will send request/response data to Redwood for model inference. Concern areas: headers (trace IDs, auth headers), whole-request bodies (medical notes), and derived embeddings.
- Primary asks from your side:
  1) Options to prevent storage of PII in logs (headers and request/response).
  2) Data residency for audit logs and raw telemetry.
  3) Retention windows and ability to purge sampled logs on demand.
  4) Evidence: SOC2 assertion + sample config/examples for redaction and retained audit fields.

What Redwood can provide (initial options)
- Header suppression profiles (remove sensitive headers by key name), optional hashing for trace IDs, or deterministic prefix truncation.
- Request/response scrubbing rules: configurable JSONPath-based redaction + regex masks for common PII patterns.
- Live prefix/KV cache option: preserve model performance while not persisting full request payloads to long-term storage.
- Retention controls: default 30d, configurable down to 0d for raw payloads; audit-only logs can be kept longer with pseudonymized identifiers.

Attachments: included a short options doc and a sample anonymized log format to illustrate what you’d see in Dev/Prod.

Asks / next steps (action items)
1) Can you confirm desired residency for logs (us-east-1 / eu-west-1 / other)?
2) Which level of header handling is acceptable: suppression | hash-trace-id | keep-as-is?
3) Please share the security contact for a formal evidence request (we’ll pull SOC2 and the minimal export of our controls).
4) If you want, we can prepare a short configuration snippet and a demo showing an end-to-end redaction pipeline.

I copied Amir in case Procurement has timing constraints. Proposed next sync: 30-minute demo on Thurs or Fri (your preference).

Thanks,

Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
Attachment stubs: redwood-telemetry-options-v1.pdf (7 pages), sample-log-format.txt (1 KB)
From: Lina Park <lina.park@medicohealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Amir Qureshi <amir.qureshi@medicohealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry & logs: PII redaction options + evidence request

Thanks Michael — quick clarifications from our side below.

Region: We prefer US residency for audit logs and telemetry (us-east-1). EU would be a blocker unless we go through an additional privacy review.

Header handling: Our default preference is hashing trace IDs (so we can correlate requests without exposing raw trace values). Suppression of auth headers is mandatory.

Retention: We need the ability to retain pseudonymized audit logs for 365 days, but raw request/response payloads must be configurable down to 0 days (we may pilot with 7-day retention).

Evidence request: Security contact is Priya Mehta (priya.mehta@medicohealth.com). She’ll want SOC2 Type II and a short technical note describing the redaction approach and where logs are retained.

Procurement timeline: we’re aiming to include this in an August procurement window — would need a finalized SOW + security addendum by July 31.

One small question: do you have a recommended approach for handling partial PII (e.g., patient initials or MRN embedded in larger free text)?

—Lina
Security Architect, MedicoHealth

Lina also asked about partial PII in free text — what’s our recommended detection/masking approach (regex + ML fallback)?

If we can prepare the config + tech note this week, I’ll schedule the short demo for Thurs.

Thanks — Michael

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry & logs: PII redaction options + evidence request

Michael / Marissa — quick technical plan and items we can hand to Priya.

1) Config snippet: I’ll prepare a YAML example showing: header_suppression: [Authorization, X-Auth-Token], trace_id: {strategy: "sha256-hex"}, redaction_rules: [{path: "$.patient.*.mrn", mode: "mask"}, {regex: "\\\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\\\b", mode: "mask"}], retention: {raw_payload_days: 7, audit_pseudonym_days: 365}.

2) Partial PII in free text: recommended two-layer approach:
   - Fast regex-based pass for common identifiers (MRN patterns, SSN-like patterns, email, phone).
   - ML classifier that flags likely PHI spans for review (we can ship a small on-premise/hosted classifier). For pilot, combine regex + lower-sensitivity ML tagger and surface masked results in demo.

3) Residency / retention: Backend supports per-tenant routing to us-east-1 for telemetry; we can enforce retention policies via lifecycle jobs. Enabling 0d retention for raw payloads is fine; note: removing raw payloads reduces our ability to run model quality regressions from production samples (call out as an operational tradeoff).

4) Evidence pack: Marissa — can you pull the SOC2 summary + the brief controls doc (we have a 1-page redaction description used for other customers). I’ll draft the tech note describing hashing vs suppression, where pseudonymized audit fields live, and the purge APIs.

Timeline: I can have the YAML snippet + draft tech note by EOD tomorrow; Marissa can attach SOC2 summary and controls page. Then Michael, you can send to Priya and book the demo.

Diego
Principal Engineer, Runtime
